transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Emma Park (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Cosmos Head of ML), Jon Rivera (Infra Lead), Alex Kim (Product)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on cost modeling and unit economics for a retrieval-augmented generation feature. Discussed workload sizing (qps, avg tokens), latency SLOs, batching and KV-caching knobs, target monthly budget, and an initial benchmarking plan. Agreed next steps: share pricing/SOW, customer to share sample prompts + traffic, Redwood to run benchmarks with suggested configs.

Topics:
- Workload profile and success criteria
- Per-token cost and effective unit economics (batching, cache hit rate)
- Benchmark plan + timeline
- Deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and cost tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, I'm Emma, AE at Redwood. Quick intro from our side, Liam's our solutions engineer, he'll handle the benchmark details.
[00:12] Maya (Cosmos): Hi all, Maya here. We run the recommendations team at Cosmos, building a question-answer feature over our analytics docs. Jon and Alex are with me.
[00:20] Jon (Cosmos): Hey, yeah hi.
[00:22] Liam (Redwood): Nice to meet you. Real quick before we dive, goal for today is to pin success criteria and get enough workload sizing to produce per-token estimates and propose batching/cache configs. Sound right?
[00:33] Maya: Yep, that's right. We're mainly worried about cost — we have a constrained budget — but can't have tail latency over 400ms for UX.
[00:40] Emma: Great, noted. Can you share current traffic numbers? QPS, average tokens per req?
[00:46] Alex (Cosmos): Our spike qps is about 25 rps for the feature, average concurrent users maybe 40; average prompt + response is around 600 tokens but it varies.
[00:57] Maya: Most calls are under a few hundred tokens but the long-run summaries push it.
[01:02] Liam: Okay 25 rps spike, avg 600 tokens, got it. For per-token estimates we need to know desired p50/p95 latency targets and whether you want hosted or private. Any constraints?
[01:15] Jon: We need SOC2 and SSO; we can go hosted if data retention and KMS integration meet our security team — otherwise private. Cost-wise, budget ceiling initially is around $15k/mo for inference.
[01:29] Emma: Thanks — that's helpful. So if we target p95 < 400ms and $15k/month, we'll run some unit economics to see if hosted fits or if dedicated makes more sense.
[01:40] Liam: Quick note on terminology: when I say KV cache I mean the prefix / attention KV cache for reused conversation context — that can dramatically cut per-token compute if hit rates are high, sometimes 30-60% savings depending on workload.
[01:53] Maya: We have a lot of repeated context — users run similar queries — so cache hit could be reasonable.
[01:58] Alex: Question — how do batching knobs affect latency?
[02:01] Liam: Good question. With batching you trade throughput for latency: larger batch sizes improve GPU utilization and lower per-token cost, but increase queuing latency. We can configure an adaptive batching policy: small latency-sensitive batches for p95 targets, and background batching for bulk ops.
[02:16] Maya: So what's a realistic per-token ballpark?
[02:18] Liam: For a hosted mixed-precision model on A100-class infra, naive generator estimate might be $0.00002 per token pre-batching; with effective batching and KV cache it can drop to $0.000008-$0.000012 per token. But that's very workload-dependent.
[02:34] Emma: Important to run a bench on your actual prompt set. We'll propose a few configs: latency-optimized hosted, cost-optimized dedicated, and hybrid with regional fallback.
[02:45] Jon: If dedicated, what's the committed spend look like?
[02:48] Liam: Dedicated usually requires a monthly commitment — initial small pool could be $8k-$12k/mo depending on GPU type and throughput. That could make sense if you need consistent 25 rps with p95 400ms and high token counts.
[03:02] Maya: Okay so tradeoff is commit vs per-token.
[03:05] Alex: For benchmarking, what data do you need from us?
[03:08] Liam: Ideally: sample prompt set (100-1k), a traffic profile with QPS distribution (peak vs baseline), and a few representative long/short requests. Also any payload size limits and SSO/KMS constraints.
[03:21] Maya: We can zip up a 500 prompt sample and traffic hist by Monday.
[03:25] Emma: Perfect. We'll then run: 1) baseline on hosted default configs, 2) latency-optimized config (small batch, low queuing), 3) cost-optimized config (aggressive batching + cache). We'll report p50/p95 latency, token/sec, and per-token cost.
[03:41] Jon: How do you compute the per-token cost in the report? Is it total infra cost / generated tokens?
[03:46] Liam: Yes, we'll show raw GPU compute cost + infra overhead amortized over tokens, then give an effective per-token number and show sensitivity to cache hit rate and batch size. We'll include assumptions like token length distribution and GPU type.
[03:59] Maya: Can you show an example calc quick?
[04:01] Liam: Sure. Example: if a workload generates 100M tokens/month and infra amortized is $2k for the period, that's $0.00002 per token baseline. If you get a 40% cache hit and batching yields 25% improvement, effective per-token might drop to ~0.00001. Those numbers are illustrative.
[04:22] Alex: Are there additional licensing fees or data egress we should consider?
[04:26] Emma: There can be platform fees for hosted usage; we'll include line items: compute, platform markup, optional observability retention. For private, there may be a software license + support fee. We'll outline that in the pricing sheet.
[04:39] Jon: Network egress could be a small extra if you host cross-region, but most of our estimate should be compute heavy.
[04:46] Liam: Also worth noting model selection matters a lot — smaller models cut cost but may drop quality. We can include a few candidate models and show nll/quality tradeoffs in the report.
[04:57] Maya: Does Redwood support quantized model variants? That could help with cost.
[05:00] Liam: Yes, we support quantization profiles; switching to int8/4 will reduce memory and sometimes increase throughput. We'll add quantized run in the benchmark plan.
[05:10] Maya: Great. On the latency SLO — p95 < 400ms — is that realistic at 25 rps?
[05:15] Liam: It's tight but achievable if average tokens aren't too large and batching is tuned for latency. We'll validate in the benchmark and recommend a config. If p95 is violated on hosted, dedicated with reserved capacity can help guarantee it.
[05:28] Emma: Also worth highlighting caching strategy: if your conversational state is reused a lot, even a small cache hit ratio reduces compute a lot. We'll simulate hit rates at 20/40/60% and show cost deltas.
[05:40] Alex: For the benchmark, how long will you run tests to get stable p95?
[05:44] Liam: We'll run steady-state for at least 15 minutes per config and some spike tests to simulate peak. That should surface queuing issues.
[05:52] Maya: Sounds good. Any red flags we should know about?
[05:55] Liam: The usual: long-tail token requests (>2k) can blow up cost; also cold KV cache or poor batching config can increase per-token pricing. We'll flag those in the report.
[06:07] Jon: Our infra team needs SSO/KMS details for security review — who owns that?
[06:12] Emma: We'll include an SSA: SSO integration (SAML), and KMS integration details in the security pack. I'll share the SOC2 docs and deployment options link.
[06:20] Alex: Any examples of similar customers?
[06:23] Emma: We have a couple of analytics customers who've run POCs with similar profiles, reduced per-token cost by ~40% with caching+batching. I'll share anonymized results.
[06:31] Maya: Good. Can you include a simple cost projection table? Like months 1-6 with expected spend under three scenarios?
[06:37] Liam: Yes we'll include three scenarios: conservative (low cache, low batching), expected, and aggressive (high cache, large batches). Each will show tokens/month, effective per-token cost, and total monthly cost.
[06:47] Maya: About timeline — when can you turn around the benchmark?
[06:50] Liam: If you share samples by Monday (2026-03-22), we can run by Wednesday and have a report by Thursday/Friday — so within 3 business days.
[06:59] Alex: That works. What about POC success criteria — what do we need to prove?
[07:03] Emma: Usually: 1) meet p95 latency target, 2) per-token cost <= your budget target ($15k/mo projected), and 3) no blocking security issues (SSO/KMS). If all three, we recommend pilot -> dedicated or scaled hosted.
[07:17] Maya: Makes sense. Can you pre-simulate cost assuming 100M tokens/month?
[07:21] Liam: Yes, we'll include that table and sensitivity to hit rates and batch sizes.
[07:25] Jon: One more infra question: for dedicated, are you able to reserve specific GPU types? We have a preference for Ampere/Streamlined ones.
[07:31] Liam: Yes we can provision dedicated pools on specific GPU classes; we'll note estimated costs for A100 vs H100 equivalents. We'll include commit tiers.
[07:40] Emma: Ok wrapping toward next steps — quick recap: Cosmos to send prompt set + traffic hist by 2026-03-22, Redwood to run benchmarks and send pricing + SOW by 2026-03-24, follow-up call to review results week of 2026-03-23.
[07:55] Maya: Confirmed. Any blockers for us?
[07:58] Emma: No blockers from our side. If you have strict KMS requirements, share early so we can validate private options.
[08:05] Jon: We'll pull the KMS and SAML details and send them with the samples.
[08:09] Liam: Quick note — for the benchmark we'll instrument token-level telemetry so you can see token split and cache hits; if you want, we'll also provide a small dashboard export.
[08:19] Alex: That would be helpful.
[08:21] Maya: Great. Anything about procurement or legal?
[08:24] Emma: I'll include a procurement timeline in the SOW; legal tends to take 2-4 weeks for enterprise deals but POC-only contracts can be expedited.
[08:33] Alex: Good to know.
[08:35] Emma: Alright if no other questions we'll close. Thanks everyone.
[08:39] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
